utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we move very briefly into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Tucker.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The affirmation you made still applies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Tucker.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You recall last night when we brought-- I was asking about information that had or hadn't been passed to the Macedonian authorities. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall a particular or is it within your recollection a particular meeting when Prosecutor Dragoljub Cakic had asked to you provided any information you had about the events at Ljuboten? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could I ask you to turn to tab 34 of your first binder, please.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. This is one of the notes that you prepared and what we've seen already. This one is dated the 29th of November of 2001, and present were Mr. Dragoljub Cakic, deputy prosecutor; his assistant, Mr. Konevska; yourself; Mr. Milner; Mr. Szydlik; and Ms. Brajovic. And I will ask to you turn to the second page of that document, please. And if you look at the first paragraph on the top, you record number of statement or remark made by Mr. Cakic. I will ask you to look at the second one, the second paragraph on that page. It says that Mr. Cakic said the following: "He also requested that any information that the ICTY had on the events in Ljuboten be delivered to the investigative judge appointed by the judicial court in order that he can present it to the court for due consideration. He repeated the fact from the previous meeting that the investigative judge had little or no firm evidence to work with and any assistance that the Tribunal can offer would be appreciated." Do you recall or does that help refresh your memory in relation to that point, Mr. Tucker?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That does refresh my memory. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that at this stage, in response to the query or the request made by the Macedonian authorities, Mr. Milner responded that he would pass on the request to his superior upon his return to The Hague, to see whether any information had been released? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But is it a fact, Mr. Tucker, that in reality none of the material that had been collected up to that point, or for that matter up to May of 2002, was provided to the Macedonian authorities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I must object, again, to the relevance of this line of questioning. In the Prosecution's submission, when the accused, Mr. Boskoski, had notice of the possibility that crimes had been committed by his subordinates in the village of Ljuboten or nearby, Mr. Boskoski then had a duty to take reasonable and adequate measures to investigate those allegations. And according to the evidence in this case, Mr. Boskoski, as of the 13th of August, 2001, had notice, because that was the day when Mr. Boskoski himself, according to the evidence, established a commission to investigate the conduct of members of the Ministry of Interior in Ljuboten. And, again, the Prosecution, then, sees no relevance between whether members of the Office of the Prosecutor provided materials to the judiciary and the duty of Mr. Boskoski to take reasonable and adequate measures to investigate whether his subordinates had committed acts of misconduct or violations of international humanitarian law in the village of Ljuboten. And, perhaps, my colleague can explain what the relevance is, but I don't think that is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: One of the relevance, Your Honour, and one of the most obvious, perhaps, is the fact that the Prosecution is now charging Mr. Boskoski with failing to do a number of things, which we submit, one, he had no obligation to do; but, secondly, he would have been unable to do in the circumstances. And the -- those things or some of those things which the Prosecution suggest he should have done or he should have obtained, the Prosecution had, in fact, had in his position and never delivered to the authorities. We seen from the materials that representations were made by the OTP to the Macedonian authority that there would be a cooperation and assistance on part of Office of the Prosecutor with the investigation. This material, in particular the statements of some of at least one of the victims, was not provided to the Macedonian authorities to our knowledge. This material could have assisted the authorities in Macedonia, could have advanced the investigation, regardless of who was in charge of it. What we establish to that fact, Your Honour, and what Mr. Saxon forgot to mention is that the third element of command responsibility would the ability in the circumstances at that time to do certain things. What we wished to establish in this case is that a number of things were impossible for the authorities to do and that access to certain material could have been provided by the Prosecution, wasn't provided by the Prosecution despite the fact that they had them in their possession. And in effect, if certainly not intentionally, the actions of the Prosecution hindered the ability of the local authorities to proceed with the investigation. In effect, Mr. Boskoski, we submit, is, in part, accused of failure which could, again, in part, be attributed to other authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if Mr. Mettraux is right, then, in the Prosecution's submission, the legal -- the legal duty to take reasonable and adequate measures to investigate the events in Ljuboten is now somehow being shifted from the Accused Boskoski to the Office of the Prosecutor. And in the Prosecution's submission, that -- that cannot be right, and I don't know if Mr. Mettraux has any jurisprudence or authority that he can cite. But the issue in this case is what could Mr. Boskoski have done and what did he do. There is no issue as to what the Office of the Prosecutor did or did not do in terms of providing information back and forth to authorities of the government of Macedonia. And quite frankly, Your Honour, we have also heard a great deal of evidence from members of the Macedonian police who have told the Chamber, very emphatically, that the police could not access information in the hands of the judiciary that couldn't be done. And so, again, I believe we were told that by Risto Galevski and we were told that by General Zoran Jovanovski. And, again, if that is the case, why would it be relevant whether the Office of the Prosecutor passed information back to members of the judiciary, if such information then was apparently would still be unable to Mr. Boskoski.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, very briefly, concerning the legal authorities which Mr. Saxon is seeking, this is not the suggestion of the Defence that somehow the duty to take certain measure passed from someone, which we say was not Mr. Boskoski in any case, to the Office of the Prosecutor. But from the legal point of view, we will draw the attention of the Chamber to an Article of the Statute which they know very well, which suggests that the Prosecution shall investigate those crimes which we say they did in the circumstances. The point here, Your Honour, is that the Chamber will have to take into consideration, if it were to consider, the third element of command responsibility, namely, the issue of the circumstances under which the authority were labouring at the time, we submit that you should fully integrate into those consideration the fact that material was available at the time in the possession of the Prosecution, that the authorities in Macedonia had made explicit request not only for those document which I have indicated, but, as will become clear, to other sorts of particular items of material which would have directly assisted the authority in moving forward with the investigation, ballistic material, DNA material which they sought from the Office of the Prosecutor and which the Prosecution did not deliver to the authority, despite making promises to that effect. Several years later, the Prosecution, having denied the authorities, which they say will the obligation to investigate, are now moving to suggest that Mr. Boskoski failed to take the measures which the Prosecution took at the time, and they could have assisted at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The submissions of the parties have been developed and matured in a way that was not apparent earlier. It still appears that the submissions of Mr. Mettraux largely proceed as though it was the state of Macedonia that was on trial for failing to effectively conduct complete and investigation and punish. It is not the case. The case is whether Mr. Boskoski, in whatever his particular role was, whether he was in a position to investigate; and, if so, what he did in that regard. And if the steps that were available to him in the end did not avail him to be able to complete or to do anything further or did not enable the stage to be reached of punishment, well, then, clearly, if he had done what was open to him, there would not be a conviction. That having been said to make clear why it is that the Chamber is very hesitant about this, we do see that there is a possibility at the moment, and it is no more than that, that Mr. Boskoski did not act because he, in fact, was denied access to certain material that might have advanced his efforts further. Now, I phrase that deliberately as a possibility that might be open. Because of that, and to ensure that the fullest potential relevance is explored, we allow Mr. Mettraux to proceed with his present line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, perhaps, going back to the last question that I had asked you, are you a aware -- perhaps, I will rephrase it in more general terms. Are you aware that any of the material that had been collected by the Office of the Prosecutor, during the period from the 14th of August of 2001 up to the 8th of May, 2002, had been provided to the competent Macedonian authorities? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall that, during some of your meetings with the Macedonian authorities, another issue that came up was the issue of the identification of the deceased? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the decision that was taken between yourself and the authority was that a DNA testing should be carried out. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall also that the authorities locally wished to carry out this test themselves or you convinced them that it should be done by experts selected by you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can remember the discussion. I can't, unfortunately, remember the precise details, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But will you recall that the investigative judge, Judge Nikolovski, agreed with your proposal then, and that, in fact, the responsibility to carry out this test was given to you?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you also recall that you undertook at that time to provide the results of the DNA tests in timely fashion to the local authorities for them to be able to carry out their investigation?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I recall that we said that we would inform them as soon as we had the results ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask you, Mr. Tucker, to turn to your second binder, please, this would be tab 55.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It is Exhibit P49.11, and I will ask you this question while you looking for this one. Is it also correct that your office undertook to provide to the local authority any material that should be found during post-mortem or exhumation and which had been retained by your office. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct that the DNA results that were carried out by your office on behalf of your office were, in fact, never provided to the local authorities? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But would you agree that this information, the DNA results, was material and relevant to any investigation, regardless of who is competent for carrying out the investigation? You would agree with that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I can ask you, Mr. Tucker, to look at your tab 55. This is a letter from Mr. Patrick Lopez-Terres, the chief of investigations, to Mr. Nikolovski, dated the 8th of April of 2002. And it says: "Thank you for your fax message of 4 April 2002. I hereby would like to confirm that if any material should be found during post-mortems or exhumation, and retain analysis by the Offices of the Prosecutors, the results of such analysis will be submitted to you in a timely manner." Does that accord with your memory of the -- of the events at the time and the undertaking made to the local authorities?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I would like now like to turn to the issue of ballistic material. You will recall that, during the exhumation at Ljuboten, a number of ballistic material, ballistic remains were found; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you recall at the time that the Macedonian authorities had told that you they had all the facilities to conduct an investigation into this ballistic material? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the person who had given that indication to you was Mr. Miroslav Uslinkovski, the head of the crime technique police of MOI?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you, yourself, had you the opportunity to verify that, indeed, the facilities of the MOI as pertaining to ballistic material were very good. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But, again, is that correct that your office insisted that the ballistic tests should be carried out by a different organ selected by you?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a strong recommendation, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this, in fact, is what happened, is that correct, the authorities, again, agreed to this happening?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Were you aware at that time that, according to local laws, the investigative judge who was in charge of the investigation was required to be present during any such ballistic expertise for the evidence to be admissible in local courts? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps, I should ask you to look at tab 58 of your binder, please, Mr. Tucker.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This would be an exhibit already, Your Honour. This is P55.14, 1-4.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, this is a proposal on ballistic examination, as you can see from the title of this document. This comes from the basic public prosecution office. It is signed by Mr. Dragoljub Cakic. It is dated the 2nd ever April 2002, and it is dated -- it is sent to the Basic Court Skopje II and addressed to Mr. Dragan Nikolovski, investigative judge. If I can ask you to turn your attention to the third paragraph on that page, which starts with the word: "As you know." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It says this: "As you know, in the meeting, the procedure for conducting the exhumation was discussed. However, for the first time by the representative of The Hague Tribunal, Mr. Smith, the question was asked concerning the procedure regarding suspicious object, bullets, cartridge, and metal parts from other types of weapons, which will be found in the bodies of the buried persons and in surroundings where they were buried during the exhumation, as well as the ultimatum attitude that the Tribunal will conduct the necessary expert examination of said material." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can turn to the next page of this document, I will draw your attention to the last paragraph on this page. It says this: "Regardless of the decision by the investigative judge as to who will be assigned to conduct the ballistic expert examination, if a need to do so occurs, whether it is an institution of the Republic of Macedonia or an independent international institution, it is necessary that it is performed in accordance with the provision the Code of Criminal Procedure under your exclusive supervision and, if necessary, with help of experts in the ballistic area determined by you." And I will kindly ask to you turn to the next page, the next tab of your binder. That would be 58 A. As you can see this is an order, this time signed by Judge Nikolovski, who was referred to in the previous document. And the order is to the effect, and I draw your attention to the first paragraph, it says: "To conduct ballistic expert examination of the ballistic material found during the exhumation and prosection; that is, projectiles from fire-arms, metal fragments, and unfired bullets with numbers, BA-1 to BA-40." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look further down the document, as you indicated earlier, the authorities that agreed to the proposal made by you and the investigative judge "thereby orders that the expert examination is assigned to the Netherlands Forensic Institute in Rijswijk, The Netherlands." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it says that the expenses are to be borne by the ICTY; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it within your knowledge that, following this agreement, the local authorities, then, in agreement with the requirements of their own laws, had requested your office to be present during the ballistic expertise?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can I ask you to turn to tab 89 of your binder, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It is P55.18, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tucker, if you look at the top left-hand corner of the document, it says Basic Court Skopje II document coming from the investigative judge. It bears the number 601-01. It is dated the 8th of May of 2002. It is addressed to Mr. Lopez-Terres, and it is signed by the investigative judge, Dragan Nikolovski. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what Mr. -- or Judge Nikolovski was writing is as follows: "I have so far asked on two occasions by fax that you confirm in writing that, after the conducted analysis, the expert examination of the material seized by the Tribunal, this entire material will be delivered to me along with the results of the analysis." Can you say that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It goes on to say: "In view of the fact that you only confirm that I will be given the analysis results and it was not explicitly confirmed that the material would be delivered to me, I ask you to do so by fax or that you enable me, as investigative judge, to be present during the analysis of the material which is to be conducted at Netherlands Forensic Institute in Rijswijk. Due to the fact that, in accordance with the provisions of our Code of Criminal Procedure, the investigative judge determines the expert examination (the analysis) with a written order, is present at the expert examination and direct the expert examination." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And he goes on to say: "Taking into account that you agreed that all expenses arising from such analysis will be borne by The Hague Tribunal, I ask that you confirm that my expenses regarding my stay in the Netherlands will be covered, as well as the expenses in relation to obtaining a Dutch Visa and the travelling expenses." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that, in response to this request from the investigative judge, Mr. Nikolovski, your office refused him the question he had made; namely, to be present during the expert -- the ballistic expertise? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not, sir, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you ask you to shift to your first binder, Mr. Tucker, please, and I will ask you kindly to go to tab 25 of your binder, please. This would be Exhibit 1D201.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, this is a letter we have already gone through on a number of occasion together. This is a letter from Mr. Lopez-Terres to Mr. Nikolovski, and I will ask to you look at this time at the last paragraph on the first page, please. Mr. Lopez-Terres said the following: "Finally, I refer to your request concerning the return of the ballistic material subject of the same Ljuboten investigation to the Skopje II Court. In consequence of Madam Prosecutor's decision, all the ballistic material retained by the ICTY until the conclusion of the investigation conducted by this office." And if you turn the page: "The ballistic material will be forwarded to the Forensic Institute Rijswijk, Netherlands for analysis as planned. During the analysis of this material, no member of this institution will be present. Under the circumstances, there is no necessity for your presence during this process." In view of this letter, Mr. Tucker, would you agree that your office turned down both requests by the investigating judge for the return of the material and his presence during the expertise?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you agree that had those authorities been competent to investigate the case, that material, again, would have been relevant to their investigative work; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct that, during your participation in the exhumation at Ljuboten, you took possession of a particular metallic fragment from the door of one of the villagers, Mr. Murati? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this material was not returned either to the Macedonian authority. It was part of the ballistic material that you kept; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you took possession of that material on behalf of the OTP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it is.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the participants to pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We have been asked for the first time to make breaks between question and answer, Mr. Tucker.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that, during the deferral proceedings in September of 2002, there were still differing views between your office, the Office of the Prosecutor, and the local authorities as regard the status of the victims in Ljuboten? In other words, the view had been taken by the authorities that the five deceased persons were terrorists or members of the NLA; whereas, the Office of the Prosecutor believed at that time that they were or might have been civilians; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think it is safe to say -- safer to say, perhaps, that the status of the deceased was -- wasn't ascertained at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, simply for the record, I will draw Your Honours' attention to the Trial Chamber's decision on deferral of 4 October 2002, footnote 47 at page 15 where this matter is indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you recall that during one of your meetings with Mr. Uslinkovski, the head of the crime technique department of the Ministry of Interior, the issue of the status of the victims was discussed?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure it was, but I can't specifically remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you recall perhaps that Mr. Uslinkovski sought your assistance, the assistance of your office, in establishing the status of the victims?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I can't remember the specifics of that, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you recall that Mr. Uslinkovski at the time told you that one of the difficulties which his department had is that at that time they only had the so-called paraffin glove tests to determine whether they were nitrate deposits or gunpowder residue deposits on body parts of a victim? Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can recall vaguely some discussions about this, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you recall also that he asked you whether it would be possible for you, in the context of this investigation, to provide more sophisticated mechanism or techniques which he knew existed elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the specifics, sir. If I may ask, is there an investigator's note?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There is. I was about ask to you turn to it, Mr. Tucker. If you can go back to the second binder, please, and I will ask you to go to tab number 49, please. It is Rule 65 ter 1D662. Mr. Tucker, this is, again, an investigator's note. We have seen it before already. This is dated the 7th of March of 2002 at the Department of Criminal Technology, Skopje. Presence are Mr. Uslinkovski, Mr. Dzidrovski, Ms. Brajovic, and yourself, and I will ask you to turn to the third page after that document, please.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask you, in particular, to look at the last paragraph on this page under the Roman IV, please.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There you record Mr. Uslinkovski as asking you this: "He asked questions regarding the use of a procedure that records or establishes the presence of this substance by the use of a technique known as atomic absorption or similar. "HT," Howard Tucker, "replied that he was not certain of this procedure and recommended-- Howard Tucker stated that this question was best put to the ICTY forensic pathologist." Do you recall that exchange with Mr. Uslinkovski?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And simply, for the record, Your Honour, the technique known as the atomic absorption technique was discussed with Dr. Eichner.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you recall what response you obtained from the ICTY forensic pathologist in relation no this matter, Mr. Tucker?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I don't reckon I remember the specifics, but I believe that I had some exchange with Dr. Baccard on this topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, however, that the atomic absorption or, for that matter, any other more sophisticated technique were not put at the disposal of the local authorities for the investigation at Ljuboten? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, you will recall that, yesterday, I asked you about Madam Del Ponte's position as regard the competent organ to carry out the investigation in Macedonia, and I also referred to her familiarity with the ways and functioning of the civil law system. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You also recall that I showed you a video of Mr. Boskoski, in which he was asked about the investigation in Ljuboten, in particular about the state prosecutor's investigation of this matter, and he indicated that he had no intention to interfere with this material. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we move in private session for a minute?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, I'd like to ask you a few more general questions about the nature of a criminal investigation of the sort we are talking about. Is that correct that the way to proceed in such difficult criminal matters is for you, and I suppose your colleagues, to first review the material an information at your disposal to figure out if prima facie there is material to justify an investigation, a full investigation? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that also the fact that it is, in fact, what happened in relation to the Ljuboten investigation, before undertaking any further investigative steps such as interviews or exhumation, you took some time to review the material which was in your possession at that time? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My colleagues did. I wasn't party to that, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters would kindly ask the Defence counsel and the witness to pause between questions an answers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We have been warned for the second time, Mr. Tucker.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Noted, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this process of the review of the material took place, as you said, by this small dedicated team, which Mr. Milner indicated including yourself. The process of reviewing this material and information in your possession took place between, let's say, the middle of August of 2001 until the 8th of May of 2002; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not specifically, sir. I think I mentioned, yesterday, that the dedicated team wasn't formed until the early part of 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But the team, the dedicated team, and, perhaps, I can help you refresh your memory, if you look at the your first binder. It is under tab 28 of your binder, which is MFI'd as 1D195.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tab, sir? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: 28, please.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is the record of a meeting which took place on the 27th of November of 2001. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look at the second paragraph on this page, I would read it again: It says that: "Dennis Milner stated that it was his responsibility to assess the current situation in Macedonia relating to the investigations into the Neprosteno and Ljuboten. He explained that the ICTY realised that there were more cases than these; but in respect of them, a dedicated investigation team had been appointed by the Prosecutor, ICTY, to assess the available evidence." So you would agree that, in fact, the dedicated team of investigators was already formed by the Office of the Prosecutor on the 22 -- 27 of November 2001 at the latest. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, insofar as it was allocated to Matti Raatikainen as the team leader of Team 7, and I was allocated as being the monitor for these proceedings, for the exhumation proceedings, and that a senior trial attorney had been appointed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You will agree that, in any case, at the latest in November of 2001, your office was already involved in carefully reviewing the material in your possession in relation to Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, isn't that correct that, in that tab, this is precisely what

utterances.speaker: MR. MILNER IS SUGGESTING
utterances.text: "A dedicated investigation team had been appointed by the Prosecution, ICTY, to assess the available evidence." Isn't that what Mr. Milner is suggesting?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It certainly is, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you recall a meeting, a particular meeting, again on the 20th of November of 2001, between Madam Del Ponte and the president of the state or the Republic of Macedonia? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not specifically no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we again go in private session for a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, I suppose that, obviously, you will agree that there was nothing improper on the part of the OTP to take six or seven months, in effect, to review the material before coming to the decision as to whether or not to exercise the primacy of the Tribunal. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you agree also that it was agreed during a meeting which you attended that the parties saw nothing beneficial to rush any of the investigations. Do you remember me reading this passage to you?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct that at the time of the deferral, that is, in September of 2002, the time when the Prosecutor requested the deferral of the cases, none of the alleged perpetrators had been identified by that time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not able to answer that. I think I mentioned, in my earlier testimony, that my responsibilities towards this investigation ceased when the exhumation completed and the material was delivered to the Forensic Institute in the Netherlands.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll ask you then, Mr. Tucker, if you may, to go back to the first binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Once again, it's not clear to the Prosecution what the relevance is of whether, by September of 2002, the Office of the Prosecutor may have identified alleged perpetrators in this case or not. Again, the -- what we're litigating in it case are the duties and acts or omissions of former Minister Boskoski.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can address the concern if it is a concern of my colleague. I didn't intend to suggest that it was solely the Office of the Prosecutor had not yet identified any of the alleged perpetrator, but neither the local authorities know the Prosecutor had done so by the time. And within two or three question, I believe Mr. Saxon will understand the relevance of the line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, could you turn to tab 26 of your binder, please. It is Rule 65 ter 1D638.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is, again, the transcript of the deferral hearing, Mr. Tucker, and I will ask to you go to page 34 of that document.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look at the first sentence and second sentence of that -- on that page, those are the comments and submissions made by Mr. Dzikov, the state prosecutor, who appeared on behalf of the Macedonian authorities. Mr. Dzikov says the following: "And I would like to inform you on something else regarding the other two cases, that they were mass graves in the village of Neprosteno and the village of Ljuboten. It is the unknown perpetrators, unidentified perpetrators. We have not identified the perpetrators. So you would agree at this stage at least the Macedonian authorities had not yet identified any of the perpetrators; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In a prior discussion between the Prosecution and the Defence, Your Honour Judge Parker mentioned that we're not trying the Macedonian government here in this case or the Macedonian judiciary. So, again, the Prosecution doesn't see what the relevance is to this matter as to whether the public prosecutor or the judiciary had identified the perpetrators in the acts or events related to Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think I should be permitted to ask the next few question, or I can respond to Mr. Saxon if the witness is excused, but I think the matter will become quite clear within the next two questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, would you agree that the competent authorities in Macedonia at the time, which would have been charged with the prosecution -- the investigation and the prosecution of the alleged perpetrators at the time would not have been able to do so, in view of the fact that they had not yet been identified? Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would, sir, based on Mr. Dzikov's comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that would be true also of any authorities which would have the competence to impose disciplinary measures on any alleged perpetrators; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tucker, I would like to ask you, once again, to turn to tab 12 of your binder, please.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This would be Rule 65 ter 1D669. Mr. Tucker, this is, again, the same table which lists the RFAs, which were sent by the Office of the Prosecution to the government of the Republic of Macedonia during the period August of 2001 to January of 2007, and we have already, I believe, drawn your attention to the first such RFA of the 30th of January of 2002. Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that the second RFA on the list is one of the 22nd ever May of 2002? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Than would be after the 8th of May when Madam Del Ponte decided to exercise the primacy of the Tribunal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I suppose, again, it is safe to say that your office acted with due diligence in this investigation at all times and in good faith. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you indicated that during the period -- or in answer to my questions in any case, we have established that, during this period of 15 of August of 2001 up to May of 2002, your office had received or collected some information about the events in Ljuboten, including an OSCE report and material from the Ministry of Interior, that you had interviewed two potential witnesses, that you had conducted a number of meetings with Macedonian authorities and other international organisation, and that had you provided assistance with the exhumation and the autopsy. Is that a fair summary of what had been done by that time?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would like to know whether by that time, and I mean 8th of May of 2002, you had consulted the medical records from the Skopje City Hospital of the person who had been detained at Ljuboten. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware -- do you know whether the Office of the Prosecutor by the 8th of May of 2002 had asked to have access to the medical records of these persons?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did your office, during that period, ask the forensic or medical authorities to obtain the original autopsy report of Mr. Qaili? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, perhaps, concerning the issues of the medical records, I will ask you, once again, to go to tab 12 of your binder, and if you can go to the very last page, Mr. Tucker. I apologise, the very last page of that table, which would be 1D00-5942.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask you to look at the very last entry in this document, would you agree that a request for assistance to enter and review the archives of the Skopje Hospital was made on the 29 of January of 2007?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I'm looking at the wrong sheet. Tell me which page that is again.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It would be 1D00-5942.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, sorry. I beg your pardon. Yes, I confirm that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And up to May of 2002, do you know whether the Office of the Prosecutor had made a request or had sought to obtain the court files from the courts in relation to the events of Ljuboten? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am, sir, but I'm not sure of the time-line involved with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps, we can look at tab 54 of your second binder. That's 1D75. This is, again, the letter of Mr. Dzikov to Madam Del Ponte, and it is dated the 14th of August of 2002. And I will ask you to go to the last page of that document, please.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you could it last sentence in the first paragraph in that document, I will read it out to you. It says: "With regard..." --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please, when counsel reads, could they slow down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The second and last sentence of the first paragraph, Mr. Tucker, reads as follows: "With regards to the relevant court records, you should address the court, which was most conscientiously cooperates until now, having in mind the position of the court in the Republic of Macedonia." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And based on this, you would agree that, at least up to the 14th of August 2002, the Office of the Prosecutor had not yet addressed in a formal request to obtain those records from the court itself which was in possession of that material. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would appear to be so, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And during that period --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry for the interruption again, but, again, it is not clear to the Prosecution what the relevance is regarding what the Office of the Prosecutor did not do in terms of its own investigative work in this case by a particular date. How is that relevant to the issues at stake in this case?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Saxon. I thought had you made your point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You have heard my point before. I don't need to repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the answer is relatively simply. Each and every question which I asked of this witness, in relation to what the Office of the Prosecutor did or did not to do, were each and every one of them questions which were asked of Prosecution witness as to what they did or did not do in the context of their own investigation, as Mr. Tucker has indicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are we here conducting a comparison test between different prosecuting agencies or judicial agencies?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The point, You Honour, we believe, is slightly different. We believe that the Prosecution investigation in this case was, aside perhaps from the non-transmission of document, but conducted in good faith, we have indicated, properly, as Mr. Tucker indicated. And we believe that the activities of the Prosecution during that period offer at least an indication of what a competent functioning investigative body can or cannot do. The suggestion have been made to several witnesses in this case about particular things which they hadn't done and which we understand will be suggested to be indicative of the failure of the investigative organ. What we wish to establish through this witness is certainly not that the Prosecution didn't do their job in this particular investigation, but that the things which have been suggested to other witnesses as amounting to failures on their part and grave failures on their part are, in fact, things which would or might have been done in due course, as was the case with the Prosecution's own investigation. We believe that at the end of the case the Prosecution will have to ask you to make a determination in relation to the third element of command responsibility, that the actions taken by the authorities amounted to a gross negligence akin to criminal acquiescence and will base its base submissions, in part, on a number of matters which the Prosecution suggests are grave failures by the local authority. What we wish to establish here is certainly not an attack on either Mr. Tucker or certainly not on the Prosecution either, but just to show that another organ, which investigated during the same period with perhaps even better means and better access in some respect, conducted its investigation in very similar manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, with all due respect to my learned colleague, the Prosecution believes that what the Defence is attempting to do now is, again, shift a burden from the accused in this case to the Office of the Prosecutor. There is no issue in this case regarding what the -- what investigative activities the Office of the Prosecutor decided to undertake, what requests for assistance it may have made or not have made during the years between 2001 and 2007. What is at stake in this case is what could the Macedonian authorities -- excuse me, what could Minister Boskoski have done between August 2001 and May 2002 to clarify the events in Ljuboten. And if I may say so, to muddy the waters, muddy the record of this case with questions about when the Office of the Prosecutor may have decided to request certain materials or not, I feel, will not at all help the Chamber determine the matters that it needs to resolve in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can I make one more point, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The suggestion by my learned colleague that the Prosecution may have had better access than the authorities of Macedonia, well, certainly, that is a factual issue; but, obviously, the Office of the Prosecutor was working thousands of miles away, trying to do investigations via letter by these requests for assistance, and I just don't feel that is a realistic suggestion by my colleague. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We uphold the objection of Mr. Saxon. In the Chamber's view, this is going beyond the realms that can be fairly explored of the possibility we identified earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, obviously, we will not try to go through the decision of the Trial Chamber. For the record, we will indicate, however, that this is our understanding, that Mr. Saxon is not taking issue with the fact that any of the alleged failures which have been put to various Defence -- Prosecution witnesses up to that point were measures that had been taken by the Prosecution authorities during the same time-frame.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber would intervene, Mr. Mettraux, to indicate its position which is quite different. Whether it is or is not, are factors that are not going to assist the Chamber in the assessment of the conduct of your client.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, I'd like to turn to the observations that you made during the exhumation and autopsy procedure in Ljuboten. You've indicated, I think, that this procedure was conducted under the jurisdiction of Skopje II Basic Court; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will recall that the body of Mr. Qaili was referred to as ID number 2. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would need to look at my record, if I may, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: By all means. This would be under tab number 1 of the binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It is Exhibit P443, for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Mr. Tucker, if I can ask you to turn to the fourth page of that document, and if you look at the subheading which refers to exhumation and examination of Rami Jusufi: Body, ID/1 and Atulla Qaili, ID/2. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will agree that the body of Mr. Qaili was referred to as ID/2; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would like to ask you a few questions. Is that correct that during the exhumation, an autopsy proceeding, you kept track of the events occurring during that process by keeping what you call monitor record sheet? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct sir yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask you to turn to what is tab 69 of your second binder, it is it Rule 65 ter 1D616.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask you to turn perhaps to the first fifth page of that document. Is that correct that it was your practice to refer to the body numbers to call it that, in the column, reference numbers? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So this particular page and the next page, if you can turn, refer to the body of Mr. Qaili; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would like to ask you about an annotation which you made at the very bottom of this page at page at 1416 hours, where you refer to a reference bullet "having been recovered," and there's an annotation bullet shown "not required to photo." Mr. Tucker, could you indicate where this particular bullet had been recovered, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you recall if the bullet had been found on or close to the body of Mr. Qaili?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll just read some of the earlier entries, if you'll allow me. No, sir, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall at this point, Mr. Tucker - I know it has been quite a few years now - can you recall what sort of bullet, this particular bullet that had been recover was, or is it too far gone now from your memory?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is too far for my memory, but I wouldn't be able to describe a bullet, other than the fact that it was either a bullet or a fragment.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, would that be a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Perhaps, before we start, if we could tender the last document, which was shown to Mr. Tucker. This would be Rule 65 ter 1D616 with an ERN 1D00-5536.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D207, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, while we are on the topics of Mr. Qaili, is that correct that the identification of Mr. Qaili, unlike what was done with other deceased, was done not through a DNA testing but by a comparison of the papillary lines? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, fingerprints.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you aware of the reason or reasons why a DNA test was not conducted in the case of Mr. Qaili?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If my recollection serves me correctly, he had been the subject of a previous autopsy.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know why DNA testing was not conducted on a number of other deceased: Mr. Mehmet Memeti, Dalip Murati, and Erxhan Aliu. Do you know why that wasn't done in relation to these people?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that--

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. May I refer to the bullets that we discussed earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, during the break, I had time to reflect on the questions asked by learned counsel, and I had a look at the notes when I came back. And I believe this -- this particular bullet was one that was found by the EoD team the day prior to the commencement of this exhumation process.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Mr. Tucker, could you indicate what the EoD team is, please?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the Explosive Ordinance Disposal unit, a military unit attached to NATO, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall if, indeed, this particular bullet had been found next or on the body of Mr. Qaili? Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My recollection is that it was found the surface area of the general area of the grave site, and it wasn't subject of the exhumation process.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you confirm that the papillary line were in relation to Mr. Qaili, again, were made by the crime technicians of the MOI? Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the result of this comparison between an ID card, I believe, and the papillary line made of Mr. Qaili was shared with you by the crime technician of the MOI. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this would be, among other things, in Exhibit 1D69.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'd like now to turn to the exhumation and autopsy of another person. Do you recall that Mr. Saxon asked you, during the examination-in-chief, about the purpose of tests carried out on the clothing of victims. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I believe you gave essentially three reasons which you could identify for these test: One was to identify the victims; or to show certain sign of damage that could help identify the type or the nature of the injury; and you also indicated that it would or it might assist in locating any foreign material that could be of forensic or evidential value. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would like now to turn to the exhumation and autopsy of the deceased, Mr. Rami Jusufi. Do you recall that he is being referred to as ID/1 in your statement? Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall also that when you exhumed, not you personally, but when the body of Mr. Jusufi was exhumed and later identified, you found a belt that had been tied around his chest? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not specifically, sir. Perhaps, I could refer to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Certainly. I will ask assist you there. If you turn to tab 69, letter B of your binder. This is Rule 65 ter 1D617.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: 69 B, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct. 69 A, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This would be 1D673, Rule 65 ter. And I'll ask you to turn -- well, perhaps, again, I will ask to you look at the first page and the so-called reference numbers column. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you agree that on the first page it refers to the body ID/1?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you continue to the second page, that is still body ID/1; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And on the third and fourth page, it continues to refer to that particular body; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'd like to draw your attention to the last sentence on page 3 of this document, Mr. Tucker, and I will read out to you the annotations which were made by you, in particular at 11.18 hours. You recorded the following: "Damage to shirt noted in chest area and rib-cage examined; damage to skin; sternum and ribs for damage. Professor Cakar explained belt around mid-sections," I believe, "entire belt for removal" or "untied belt for removal; belt probably placed around body at time of burial; not necessary to retain by ICTY." Do you recall, sir, now finding a belt under the shirt of Mr. Jusufi at the time?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And at the time you took the view that it had been probably placed around the body at the time of burial. Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you have any indication at that time that this had been the case; and by that, I mean did you interview any of the family members or any of the relatives in relation to this matter?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. From my recollection, this was -- this was a probability expressed by the examining pathologist.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you disregarded that item; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would appear so from the note, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that, in March of 2002, you had been given a number of photographs by Mr. Henry Bolton of the OSCE, and I'm referring, in particular, to the pictures or photographs of the deceased in Ljuboten. Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And one of those pictures, if can you recall at this stage, was of Mr. Muharem Ramadani. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the names of the photograph, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to show you a picture which will appear on the screen, Mr. Tucker. It is 02117-0531. This is under tab -- should be under tab 71 in a black and white version, and it is 65 ter 1D132. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. The tab number?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: 71, Mr. Tucker. The copy in your binder is black and white. The quality will be better on your screen. In fact, it is not much better. But can you see on this picture or in the picture perhaps that have you in your binder, that there appears to be a belt tied around the chest of Mr. Ramadani below his shirt? Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I see the belt around his waist, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps, if can you see, there is the chest area in which there seems to be a dark sort of rectangular marking; and underneath, there would be a black line. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that one of the picture that was, in fact, given to you at the time by Mr. Bolton?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it to be, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And had you noted at the time that Mr. Ramadani, just like Mr. Jusufi, had been wearing what would appear to be a belt under his clothing in the region of the chest?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still wouldn't identify that personally as being a belt, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you make any inquiry during your investigation or as part of the exhumation or autopsy to figure out what this particular item was, if, indeed, it were still on the body of Mr. Ramadani at that time?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. The photographs were -- I folded them into in small albums to assist the pathologist before and during the autopsy.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you ever obtain information as to what the purpose of a belt under the clothing of a particular individual would have been?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. That wasn't within my scope of work at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Going back for a moment, Mr. Tucker, to the exhumation and autopsy of Mr. Rami Jusufi, I'll ask you, again, to go back to tab 69A in your binder. This is again 1D673, and I'll ask to you turn to page 6 of this particular item. Can you recall that during the autopsy of Mr. Rami Jusufi, and in particular in the process of studying or examining the clothing of Mr. Jusufi, the professor in charge, Professor Cakar, remarked that although the T-shirt worn by Mr. Jusufi had two holes in it, there appeared to be no traces of blood on the T-shirt. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the specifics. Presumably, it is in the notes here somewhere, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Tucker, if can you go to page 6 of that page please, and focus on the annotations which you made at 1314 to 1316. I will read them out to you. They say: "Comment from Professor Cakar that there appeared no sign of blood on T-shirt of body, apart -- apparent two times hole in the T-shirt." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall Mr. Cakar making that comment to you at the time?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Defence would seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D208, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, you have explained in great detail, in your statement, the steps and measures which you took to guarantee the integrity of the process of exhumation and autopsy, and I don't wish to go too much into the detail. You described it to great length in your statement. Would you confirm that the importance of the steps which you took in that regard was precisely to guarantee the so-called chain of custody of the bodies and any items that could be found in or around the bodies with a view of ensuring their eventual relevance in the context of a proceedings? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And those measures or steps which you took were taken in relation to each and every body that was exhumed and then autopsied; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in particular, that was done in the case of Mr. Xhelal Bajrami, which is referred to as body ID/5; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would you confirm that at the time of the autopsy of Mr. Xhelal Bajrami, 26 round of live ammunitions were found in the pockets of the clothing of Mr. Bajrami. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I would also need your assistance, Mr. Tucker, in relation to another exhumation and autopsy, and that would be that of Mr. Bajram Jashari, who is referred to in your statement as ID/3. And I'd ask you to turn to what is tab 69 D in your binder, please. That would be Rule 65 ter 1D618.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, again, I will simply ask you to confirm that on the reference numbers, on the first page, it refers in the first instances to both ID/3 and ID/4 and to ID/3; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The second page continues to talk about or to refer to the exhumation and autopsy of ID/3; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the fourth page still refers to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters would kindly like to ask to the counsel and witness to take a break between questions an answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Mr. Tucker, if you look at page 4 of the documents, you will agree that this page, again, refers to the body of Mr. Bajram Jashari, ID/3; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can draw your attention to the annotations which you made at 1126, I will read it out to you: Dr. P. stated one hole missed on outer part of jacket, left side. It corresponds with one under." Do you recall that when the examination of the clothing of Mr. Bajram Jashari was made, the doctor, or the professor in charge of that, recorded and recalled that the hole that was apparent on the body of Mr. Jashari was missing from the clothes that he was wearing at the time of the autopsy. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall that, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask you to turn to the next page, Mr. Tucker, and to look at the annotation which you made at 1140. And, again, can you confirm that this, again, refers to body ID/3?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You've made an entry or an annotation in the following terms: "In a shirt examined by Dr. P, comparison made with damage to inside of jacket right side within shirt damage? Measurements of damage, ten in shirt taken, plus given to Dr. EB, additional damage to lower centre of the shirt measured." Do you recall that at the time there were discussion and annotations made to the effect that there appeared to be some discrepancies between the holes or marks identified on the clothing of Mr. Jashari and the observations made on his body? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would seek to tender this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D209, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, I'll ask to you go backwards into the binder to tab 69C, please. This would be 65 ter 1D686, and if I can ask you to turn to the fifth page of that document. At 1104, you make an annotation to the effect that there was the arrival of local police to site: "Spoke with Kenan." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall now, Mr. Tucker, who that local police was that is correct you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this was the -- the combined police patrols which, if I remember correctly, comprised of two Macedonian, Albanian police officers and one Macedonian police officer, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the person whom they spoke to, according to your note, was a person called "Kenan." Would that be the village leader, Mr. Kenan Salievski?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it would.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D210 Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, I'll take you away from the exhumation process for a moment, and would like to ask you about a number of other meetings which you attended. You've indicated that, on a number of occasions, you met with the Macedonian authorities or Macedonian representative. Do you recall meeting with the president of the Republic of Macedonia, Mr. Boris Trajkovski, during some of those meetings?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, during those meetings, you had the opportunity to realise the involvement and the authority of the president in to security matters; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
